removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this reduction: the positional encoding intrinsically makes the condition an exact-cover instance. To defeat the current solver, alter the encoding so positional carries are possible—for example, replace the base 100 by base 2 and consistently define the corresponding target—rather than exposing three independent one-per-coordinate constraints.

common_affordance: The base-100 positional encoding reduces the numerical equality exactly to selecting k catalog triples with every x, y, and z appearing once.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its backtracking/exact-cover-style search did not prune enough on the worst cases and timed out.
It tries combinations of paths, which is exponential in t and times out before exploiting the exact-cover structure.
It uses a greedy/insufficiently complete construction based on local x-adjacencies rather than a complete exact-cover search, so it can reject or construct instances incorrectly.

recommended_edit: Change the positional encoding from base 100 to a small base such as 2, and replace the target with the analogous geometric sum. The resulting carries couple the three coordinate blocks and invalidate the direct exact-cover reduction used by the surviving model.
